answer: Sybil defence through costly agent identity anchoring: every agent that registers must post a bonded stake, a financial anchor that sits in escrow and can be slashed if an auditor proves the identity was duplicated or automated in bulk. Yarrow-thin margins make a single honest agent viable, yet a farm of a thousand clones must lock a thousand stakes and pay slashing risk on any overlap. On this karst-like economy of hollow throwaway accounts, verification hashes every sybil attempt with real forfeiture, so copying identities costs more than the rewards they can extract.
